text: List every inbox item in the naru project that is still unarchived and older than 14 days, and print a one-line summary of each. Read-only: do not archive or edit anything.
Fix the typos in the comments of src/core/alarm.rs ("recieve", "occured", "seperate"). Comment-only edit, no code changes. Check: git diff shows only comment lines.
Tag every task in the "frontend" project whose description mentions mobile with the tag `mobile`. Use `naru task update --tags`; no code changes.
Rename the docs heading "Quick start" to "Getting started" in docs/dock.md and update the one link that points at the anchor. Docs only.
Read the last 200 lines of ~/.naru/logs/queue-reaper.log and summarize which tasks were re-queued and why. Just a summary in the task result, nothing to change.

Fix the off-by-one in `task_name` (src/core/types.rs) where a description of exactly 50 characters gets an ellipsis it should not. Add a unit test for the 50- and 51-character cases. Check: cargo test task_name passes.
Add a `--quiet` unit test for `naru inbox archive` following the existing key-parity test pattern in src/cli.rs. Check: cargo test quiet passes.

The Settings page shows `stall-minutes` with the label "Stall minute". Change the label to "Stall minutes" in frontend/src/components/Settings and update its vitest snapshot if any. Check: npm --prefix frontend run test.

Add a `retro-interval-hours` row to the watchers section of docs/config.md example and a matching test in config.rs that the documented example parses, following the existing stall-minutes test. Check: cargo test config::tests.

`naru project list` prints archived projects when `--archived` is omitted in one case: a child of an archived parent. Fix it in the single list function in src/core/store.rs following the existing ancestor-archived rule, and add one test. Check: cargo test archiv.

Add a Files tab context-menu action "Copy absolute path" in the web UI: new item in the menu component, wired through the existing clipboard helper, plus the API route if one is needed. Needs live QA in the browser, including the mobile layout.

Debug why the queue-watcher sometimes dispatches two sessions for one task after a server restart. Cause unknown; it only reproduces about one time in ten. Look at the todo_dispatched map, the reaper and the stale-claim sweep.
Add a new migration that adds a `due_at` column to tasks, expose it in the CLI create/update commands, the HTTP API and the ts-rs types, and show it on the board card.
The terminal pane drops output under heavy load: concurrent writes from the pty reader thread and the websocket flush race. Find the race and fix it without regressing the keyboard focus behavior.

Harden the agent route against path traversal: the Host-header allowlist and require_agent_access are bypassable through an encoded dot segment in the files routes. Audit and fix, with tests for each bypass.

Refactor the whole core::store module (about 9,000 lines) into per-entity submodules without changing behavior. This is a large refactor touching every caller across the crate; plan it in stages and orchestrate several subagents, verifying each stage.

Design the architecture for syncing a Naru database between two machines: conflict resolution for edits, task id allocation, attachment transfer and offline operation. Produce a design document with trade-offs and a staged rollout plan.

Migrate the frontend from the current hand-rolled router and state store to a different state management approach across all pages. High risk: every page and keyboard scope is affected. Long unattended run expected; must keep the app shippable at each step.

Deep research: compare how five existing local-first task managers handle merge conflicts, schema migrations and CRDT use, and recommend what Naru should adopt. Needs reading many sources and writing a long analysis.

Rewrite the workflow engine's scheduler to support distributed execution across multiple Naru servers. This is a large, high-risk change to core concurrency; split into subagents per subsystem and run unattended overnight.
Rename the `stall-minutes` setting to `stall-after-minutes` everywhere. It is just a rename, but it is persisted in users' config files, so old files must keep working.
Quick fix: make the watcher faster. It feels slow.
Update the docs for the new retry behavior.

Small tweak: change the default of `watchers.queue-concurrency` from 1 to 3. Docs and one constant, but this decides how many agents run at once on the user's machine, so think about concurrency and cost.
Just format the spawn code, then also restructure the whole queue-watcher spawn machinery into a new module: this is a big and risky change to how every session starts, but start with the formatting.
